content.en: The **International Development Association (IDA)** is the concessional lending arm of the World Bank. Unlike the IBRD, which lends to middle-income countries, the IDA focuses on the poorest nations. It provides **credits** (interest-free loans) and **grants** to support projects that boost economic growth, reduce inequalities, and improve people's living conditions.

definition.en: Loans provided with zero or very low interest rates and long repayment periods.

content.en: IDA resources are replenished every three years by donor countries.

content.en: Confusing IDA with IBRD; remember IDA is for the poorest countries, while IBRD serves middle-income countries.
